content.introduction: The United States Inflation Rate increased to 3.70 percent in September from 3.40 percent in August of 2026, according to Trading Economics and U.S. Labor Department data. The annual inflation rate accelerated to 3.7% in September 2026, driven by higher energy prices, with gasoline rising 34.2% year-over-year and fuel oil prices increasing 74.2%. The sources do not provide a definitive answer for the inflation rate beyond September 2026.
body: ## Inflation Rate in the United States increased to 3.70 percent in September from 3.40 percent in August of 2026. Inflation Rate in the United States averaged 3.29 percent from 1914 until 2026, reaching an all time high of 23.70 percent in June of 1920 and a record low of -15.80 percent in June of 1921. United States Inflation Rate - data, historical [...] ### Inflation Rate in the United States increased to 3.70 percent in September from 3.40 percent in August of 2026. Inflation Rate in the United States is expected to be 3.40 percent by the end of this quarter, according to Trading Economics global macro models and analysts expectations. In the long-term, the United States Inflation Rate is projected to trend around 2.60 percent in 2027 and 2.50 percent in 2028, according to our econometric models. [...] ## The US annual inflation rate accelerated to 3.7% in September 2026, up from 3.4% in each of the previous two months and above market expectations of 3.6%, driven by higher energy prices. Gasoline rose 34.2% yoy, more than 27.4% in August and fuel oil prices increased 74.2%, compared with 52% previously. The US Inflation Rate is the percentage in which a chosen basket of goods and services purchased in the US increases in price over a year. Inflation is one of the metrics used by the US Federal Reserve to gauge the health of the economy. Since 2012, the Federal Reserve has targeted a 2% inflation rate for the US economy and may make changes to monetary policy if inflation is not within that range. A notable time for inflation was the early 1980's during the recession.
